## Data S6: Supplementary File 6 Analysis of Evo-designed phage genomes.xlsx
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Data S6: Analysis of Evo-designed phage genomes
# ============================================================

# 1. Load required packages
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)


# 2. Define supplementary data file
file_path <- paste0(
  "./codes_Github_final/Supplementary_Data/",
  "Supplementary File 6 Analysis of Evo-designed phage genomes.xlsx"
)

stopifnot(file.exists(file_path))


# 3. Load all worksheets
sheet_names <- readxl::excel_sheets(file_path)

data_s6 <- purrr::map(
  sheet_names,
  ~ readxl::read_excel(
    file_path,
    sheet = .x,
    guess_max = 10000
  )
)

names(data_s6) <- sheet_names


# 4. Inspect workbook
names(data_s6)

purrr::map(data_s6, dim)

purrr::map(data_s6, names)




```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Prepare nucleotide mutational-effect summary
# ============================================================

prepare_stacked_percent_data <- function(
    data,
    class_var,
    category_var,
    facet_var = NULL
) {

  class_var <- rlang::ensym(class_var)
  category_var <- rlang::ensym(category_var)

  if (is.null(facet_var)) {

    summary_df <- data %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(!!class_var),
        !is.na(!!category_var)
      ) %>%
      dplyr::count(
        !!class_var,
        !!category_var,
        name = "count"
      ) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(!!class_var) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        total_count = sum(count),
        percent = 100 * count / total_count
      ) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup()

    total_df <- summary_df %>%
      dplyr::distinct(
        !!class_var,
        total_count
      )

    return(
      list(
        summary_df = summary_df,
        total_df = total_df
      )
    )
  }

  facet_var <- rlang::ensym(facet_var)

  summary_df <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(!!class_var),
      !is.na(!!category_var),
      !is.na(!!facet_var)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::count(
      !!facet_var,
      !!class_var,
      !!category_var,
      name = "count"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      !!facet_var,
      !!class_var
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      total_count = sum(count),
      percent = 100 * count / total_count
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  total_df <- summary_df %>%
    dplyr::distinct(
      !!facet_var,
      !!class_var,
      total_count
    )

  list(
    summary_df = summary_df,
    total_df = total_df
  )
}

nt_effect_context_plot_data <-
  prepare_stacked_percent_data(
    data = evo_nt_analysis %>%

# ============================================================
# Plot donut plots showing proportions
# ============================================================

plot_donut_percent <- function(
    df,
    category_col = Category,
    count_col = count,
    percent_col = NULL,
    title = "Composition",
    label_acc = 0.1,
    palette = NULL,
    show_count = FALSE
) {

  cat_sym <- rlang::enquo(category_col)
  cnt_sym <- rlang::enquo(count_col)
  pct_sym <- rlang::enquo(percent_col)

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Collapse to category level
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (!rlang::quo_is_null(pct_sym)) {

    df_cat <- df %>%
      dplyr::group_by(!!cat_sym) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(
        percent = sum(!!pct_sym, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        percent = dplyr::if_else(
          percent > 1,
          percent / 100,
          percent
        ),
        count = NA_integer_
      )

  } else {

    df_cat <- df %>%
      dplyr::group_by(!!cat_sym) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(
        count = sum(!!cnt_sym, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        percent = count / sum(count)
      )
  }

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Labels
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (show_count) {

    df_cat <- df_cat %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        label = paste0(
          scales::percent(
            percent,
            accuracy = label_acc
          ),
          "\n(n=",
          scales::comma(count),
          ")"
        )
      )

  } else {

    df_cat <- df_cat %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        label = scales::percent(
          percent,
          accuracy = label_acc
        )
      )
  }

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Donut
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    df_cat,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = 2,
      y = percent,
      fill = !!cat_sym
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(
      color = "white",
      width = 0.9
    ) +
    ggplot2::coord_polar(
      theta = "y"
    ) +
    ggplot2::xlim(
      0.5,
      2.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      ggplot2::aes(
        label = label
      ),
      position = ggplot2::position_stack(
        vjust = 0.5
      ),
      size = 4
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = title,
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL,
      fill = rlang::as_name(cat_sym)
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_void() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      legend.position = "none"
    )

  if (!is.null(palette)) {

    p <- p +
      ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
        values = palette,
        drop = FALSE
      )
  }

  p
}


# ============================================================
# Stacked bar plot
# Updated: make plot_stacked_bar() aggregate count internally according to the dimensions actually being plotted
# - internally aggregates counts
# - recalculates totals and percentages
# ============================================================

plot_stacked_bar <- function(
    summary_df,
    total_df = NULL,
    class_name,
    category_name,
    fill_values,
    fill_legend_title,
    plot_title = NULL,
    x_label = "Class",
    y_label = NULL,
    facet_name = NULL,
    x_text_angle = 45,
    y_type = c("percent", "count"),
    show_total_labels = TRUE,
    aggregate_counts = TRUE
) {

  y_type <- match.arg(y_type)


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Internally aggregate counts
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (aggregate_counts) {

    grouping_vars <- c(
      class_name,
      category_name
    )

    # If faceting, retain facet as part of grouping
    if (!is.null(facet_name)) {
      grouping_vars <- c(
        facet_name,
        grouping_vars
      )
    }


    summary_df <- summary_df %>%

      dplyr::group_by(
        dplyr::across(
          dplyr::all_of(
            grouping_vars
          )
        )
      ) %>%

      dplyr::summarise(
        count = sum(
          count,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        .groups = "drop"
      )


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Recalculate totals
    #
    # Without facet:
    #   total per class
    #
    # With facet:
    #   total per class within each facet
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    total_group_vars <- class_name

    if (!is.null(facet_name)) {
      total_group_vars <- c(
        facet_name,
        class_name
      )
    }


    total_df <- summary_df %>%

      dplyr::group_by(
        dplyr::across(
          dplyr::all_of(
            total_group_vars
          )
        )
      ) %>%

      dplyr::summarise(
        total_count = sum(
          count,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        .groups = "drop"
      )


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Recalculate percentages
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    summary_df <- summary_df %>%

      dplyr::left_join(
        total_df,
        by = total_group_vars
      ) %>%

      dplyr::mutate(
        percent =
          100 * count / total_count
      )
  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Select Y variable
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (y_type == "percent") {

    y_var <- "percent"

    if (is.null(y_label)) {
      y_label <- "Proportion (%)"
    }

  } else {

    y_var <- "count"

    if (is.null(y_label)) {
      y_label <- "Count"
    }
  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Base plot
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    summary_df,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = .data[[class_name]],
      y = .data[[y_var]],
      fill = .data[[category_name]]
    )
  ) +

    ggplot2::geom_col(
      position = "stack",
      width = 0.9,
      color = "black"
    ) +

    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
      values = fill_values,
      name = fill_legend_title,
      drop = FALSE
    ) +

    ggplot2::labs(
      title = plot_title,
      x = x_label,
      y = y_label
    ) +

    ggplot2::theme_classic() +

    ggplot2::theme(

      axis.text.x =
        ggplot2::element_text(
          angle = x_text_angle,
          hjust =
            ifelse(
              x_text_angle == 0,
              0.5,
              1
            )
        ),

      strip.background =
        ggplot2::element_blank(),

      strip.text =
        ggplot2::element_text(
          face = "bold"
        )
    )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Y-axis
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (y_type == "percent") {

    p <- p +

      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        breaks = seq(
          0,
          100,
          25
        ),
        expand = c(
          0,
          0
        )
      ) +

      ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
        ylim = c(
          0,
          110
        ),
        clip = "off"
      )

  } else {

    p <- p +

      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        expand =
          ggplot2::expansion(
            mult = c(
              0,
              0.12
            )
          )
      )
  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Total labels
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (show_total_labels) {

    if (y_type == "percent") {

      p <- p +

        ggplot2::geom_text(
          data = total_df,

          ggplot2::aes(
            x = .data[[class_name]],
            y = 105,
            label =
              scales::comma(
                total_count
              )
          ),

          inherit.aes = FALSE,
          size = 3.5,
          vjust = 0
        )

    } else {

      p <- p +

        ggplot2::geom_text(
          data = total_df,

          ggplot2::aes(
            x = .data[[class_name]],
            y = total_count,
            label =
              scales::comma(
                total_count
              )
          ),

          inherit.aes = FALSE,
          size = 3.5,
          vjust = -0.4
        )
    }
  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Faceting
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (!is.null(facet_name)) {

    p <- p +

      ggplot2::facet_wrap(
        stats::as.formula(
          paste(
            "~",
            facet_name
          )
        ),
        ncol = 1
      )
  }


  p
}

# ============================================================
# Identify substitution-only viable isolates
# ============================================================

substitution_only_isolates <-
  evo_nt_analysis %>%
  dplyr::group_by(isolate) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_substitutions = sum(
      mutation_type == "substitution",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    n_other_mutations = sum(
      is.na(mutation_type) |
      mutation_type != "substitution"
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    n_substitutions > 0,
    n_other_mutations == 0
  ) %>%
  dplyr::pull(isolate) %>%
  as.character()


# Preserve metadata order
substitution_only_isolate_order <-
  evo_isolate_order[
    evo_isolate_order %in%
      substitution_only_isolates
  ]


# Inspect selected isolates
print(substitution_only_isolates)
```

### 2) ~300 evo-designed genomes (Fig. S8B, C)
```{r}

# ============================================================
# Data S6: Analysis of ~300 Evo-designed phage genomes
# ============================================================

# 1. Extract supplementary datasets
evo300_nt_analysis <-
  data_s6[["Evo300_all_mutations"]]

evo300_viability_predictors <-
  data_s6[["Evo300_genome_summary"]]


# 2. Inspect datasets
dim(evo300_nt_analysis)
dim(evo300_viability_predictors)

names(evo300_nt_analysis)
names(evo300_viability_predictors)


# 3. Check genome identifiers
dplyr::n_distinct(
  evo300_viability_predictors$original_design_id
)

dplyr::n_distinct(
  evo300_nt_analysis$original_design_id
)


# 4. Inspect viability and synthesis status
table(
  evo300_viability_predictors$rebooting_viable,
  useNA = "ifany"
)
# FALSE  TRUE  <NA> 
#   269    16    17 

table(
  evo300_viability_predictors$failed_DNA_synthesis,
  useNA = "ifany"
)
# FALSE  TRUE 
#   285    17 


# 5. Inspect similarity bins
table(
  evo300_viability_predictors$nearest_natural_similarity_bin,
  useNA = "ifany"
)
#    <90  90–92  92–94  94–96  96–98 98–100 
#    184     14     23     35     33     13 



# ============================================================
# Panel A: Strongly detrimental mutations vs natural similarity
# ============================================================

# 1. Define similarity bin order
similarity_bin_order <- c(
  "<90",
  "90–92",
  "92–94",
  "94–96",
  "96–98",
  "98–100"
)


# 2. Prepare genome-level data
evo300_panelA_data <-
  evo300_viability_predictors %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    failed_DNA_synthesis == FALSE,
    !is.na(rebooting_viable),
    is.finite(prop_strongly_detrimental),
    !is.na(nearest_natural_similarity_bin)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    viability_state = dplyr::case_when(
      rebooting_viable &
        dplyr::coalesce(
          acquired_mutations_during_rebooting,
          FALSE
        ) ~
        "Viable after acquired mutation(s)",

      rebooting_viable ~ "Viable",

      TRUE ~ "Nonviable"
    ),

    nearest_natural_similarity_bin = factor(
      nearest_natural_similarity_bin,
      levels = similarity_bin_order
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(nearest_natural_similarity_bin)
  )


# 3. Check included genomes
evo300_panelA_data %>%
  dplyr::count(
    nearest_natural_similarity_bin,
    viability_state
  )


# 4. Median proportion within each similarity bin
evo300_panelA_bin_summary <-
  evo300_panelA_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    nearest_natural_similarity_bin
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_genomes = dplyr::n(),

    median_prop_strongly_detrimental = median(
      prop_strongly_detrimental,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


print(evo300_panelA_bin_summary)
# # A tibble: 6 × 3
#   nearest_natural_similarity_bin n_genomes median_prop_strongly_detrimental
#   <fct>                              <int>                            <dbl>
# 1 <90                                  177                           0.230 
# 2 90–92                                 14                           0.136 
# 3 92–94                                 20                           0.0909
# 4 94–96                                 31                           0.0602
# 5 96–98                                 30                           0.0245
# 6 98–100                                13                           0.0122



# ============================================================
# Panel A: Plot (presented Fig. S8C)
# ============================================================

# Determine space for n labels
panelA_y_max <- max(
  evo300_panelA_data$prop_strongly_detrimental,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

panelA_label_y <- max(
  panelA_y_max * 1.07,
  panelA_y_max + 0.025
)

p_panelA <-
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    evo300_panelA_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = nearest_natural_similarity_bin,
      y = prop_strongly_detrimental
    )
  ) +

  # Nonviable genomes
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(
    data = evo300_panelA_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        viability_state == "Nonviable"
      ),

    width = 0.18,
    height = 0,

    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.5,
    color = "black"
  ) +

  # Viable genomes
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(
    data = evo300_panelA_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        viability_state != "Nonviable"
      ),

    ggplot2::aes(
      fill = viability_state
    ),

    width = 0.18,
    height = 0,

    shape = 21,
    size = 3.2,
    stroke = 0.6,
    color = "black"
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Viable" = "#A8D5A2",

      "Viable after acquired mutation(s)" = "#F2C879"
    ),

    name = NULL
  ) +

  # Median within each similarity bin
  ggplot2::geom_crossbar(
    data = evo300_panelA_bin_summary,

      ymin = median_prop_strongly_detrimental,
      ymax = median_prop_strongly_detrimental
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    width = 0.45,
    linewidth = 0.5,
    color = "red"
  ) +

  # Number of genomes per similarity bin
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = evo300_panelA_bin_summary,

    ggplot2::aes(
      x = nearest_natural_similarity_bin,
      y = panelA_label_y,
      label = paste0("n=", n_genomes)
    ),

    size = 3.5
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(

    )

    ylim = c(

      panelA_label_y * 1.05
    ),
    clip = "off"
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(

    y = "Fraction of strongly detrimental substitutions"
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme_classic() +

  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "top"
  )

# 1. Prepare genome classifications
evo300_strongly_detrimental_by_genome <-
  evo300_viability_predictors %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    failed_DNA_synthesis == FALSE,
    !is.na(rebooting_viable),
    !is.na(contains_strongly_detrimental)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    viability = dplyr::if_else(
      rebooting_viable,
      "Viable",
      "Nonviable"
    ),

    strongly_detrimental_status = dplyr::if_else(
      contains_strongly_detrimental,
      "≥1 strongly detrimental SNV",
      "No strongly detrimental SNV"
    ),

    viability = factor(
      viability,
      levels = c(
        "Nonviable",
        "Viable"
      )
    ),

    strongly_detrimental_status = factor(
      strongly_detrimental_status,
      levels = c(
        "≥1 strongly detrimental SNV",
        "No strongly detrimental SNV"
      )
    )
  )


# 2. Count genomes by viability and mutation status
evo300_panelB_data <-
  evo300_strongly_detrimental_by_genome %>%
  dplyr::count(
    viability,
    strongly_detrimental_status,
    name = "n_genomes"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    viability,
    strongly_detrimental_status,
    fill = list(n_genomes = 0L)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    viability
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_total = sum(n_genomes),

    fraction = n_genomes / n_total,

    percent = 100 * fraction
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()


# 3. Inspect results
print(evo300_panelB_data)
```

### 3) Lytic performance (Fig. S8D)
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Data S6: Mutational features vs. lytic performance
# ============================================================

evo16_correlation_data_actual <-
  data_s6[["Evo16_lytic_performance"]]

# Inspect dataset

# Check isolates
unique(evo16_correlation_data_actual$isolate)

# Check mutation acquisition
table(

# FALSE  TRUE 
#     9     7 


# ============================================================
# Define predictors and panel labels
# ============================================================

plot_spec_8 <- tibble::tibble(
  predictor = c(
    "n_detrimental",
    "prop_detrimental",
    "median_fitness_detrimental",
    "n_strongly_detrimental",
    "prop_strongly_detrimental",
    "median_fitness_strongly_detrimental",
    "min_DMS_fitness",
    "nearest_natural_sequence_similarity"
  ),

  panel_group = c(
    "Detrimental",
    "Detrimental",
    "Detrimental",
    "Strongly detrimental",
    "Strongly detrimental",
    "Strongly detrimental",
    "Whole-DMS data",
    "Baseline"
  ),

  panel_metric = c(
    "Number",
    "Fraction",
    "Median fitness",
    "Number",
    "Fraction",
    "Median fitness",
    "Minimum fitness",
    "Similarity (%)"
  )
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    panel_label = paste0(
      panel_group, "\n", panel_metric
    )
  )


# Original 4 x 2 panel order
desired_panel_order <- c(
  "Detrimental\nNumber",
  "Detrimental\nFraction",
  "Detrimental\nMedian fitness",
  "Whole-DMS data\nMinimum fitness",
  "Strongly detrimental\nNumber",
  "Strongly detrimental\nFraction",
  "Strongly detrimental\nMedian fitness",
  "Baseline\nSimilarity (%)"
)


# Check required columns before plotting
required_cols <- c(
  "isolate",
  "acquired_mutations_during_rebooting",
  "GrowthRateMin_mean",
  plot_spec_8$predictor
)

setdiff(
  required_cols,
  names(evo16_correlation_data_actual)
)
# character(0)


# ============================================================
# Prepare Evo16 scatter-plot data
# ============================================================

stopifnot(
  all(required_cols %in%
        names(evo16_correlation_data_actual))
)

evo16_scatter_long <-
  purrr::map_dfr(
    seq_len(nrow(plot_spec_8)),
    function(i) {

      this_predictor <- plot_spec_8$predictor[i]

      evo16_correlation_data_actual %>%
        dplyr::transmute(
          isolate,
          acquired_mutations_during_rebooting,
          GrowthRateMin_mean,

          predictor = this_predictor,

          panel_group = plot_spec_8$panel_group[i],
          panel_metric = plot_spec_8$panel_metric[i],
          panel_label = plot_spec_8$panel_label[i],

          x = .data[[this_predictor]]
        )
    }
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    viability_display = dplyr::case_when(
      acquired_mutations_during_rebooting %in% TRUE ~
        "Viable after acquired mutation(s)",

      TRUE ~ "Viable"
    ),

    panel_label = factor(
      panel_label,
      levels = desired_panel_order
    )
  )


# Keep complete observations for each predictor
evo16_scatter_plot_data <-
  evo16_scatter_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    is.finite(x),
    is.finite(GrowthRateMin_mean)
  )


# Inspect sample sizes
evo16_scatter_plot_data %>%
  dplyr::count(
    panel_label,
    name = "n"
  )
# # A tibble: 8 × 2
#   panel_label                                n
#   <fct>                                  <int>
# 1 "Detrimental\nNumber"                     16
# 2 "Detrimental\nFraction"                   16
# 3 "Detrimental\nMedian fitness"             16
# 4 "Whole-DMS data\nMinimum fitness"         16
# 5 "Strongly detrimental\nNumber"            16
# 6 "Strongly detrimental\nFraction"          16
# 7 "Strongly detrimental\nMedian fitness"     9
# 8 "Baseline\nSimilarity (%)"                16


# ============================================================
# Calculate Spearman correlations
# ============================================================

# Common y-axis range
growth_min <- min(
  evo16_scatter_plot_data$GrowthRateMin_mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

growth_max <- max(
  evo16_scatter_plot_data$GrowthRateMin_mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

growth_range <- growth_max - growth_min

if (growth_range == 0) {
  growth_range <- 1
}

# Reserve space above data points for statistics
stats_y_pos <- growth_max + 0.12 * growth_range


# Calculate correlations
evo16_scatter_stats <-
  evo16_scatter_plot_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    predictor,
    panel_group,
    panel_metric,
    panel_label
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(
    ~ {

      df <- .x

      n <- nrow(df)

      if (
        n >= 3 &&
        dplyr::n_distinct(df$x) > 1 &&
        dplyr::n_distinct(df$GrowthRateMin_mean) > 1
      ) {

        test <- suppressWarnings(
          stats::cor.test(
            df$x,
            df$GrowthRateMin_mean,
            method = "spearman",
            exact = FALSE
          )
        )

        rho <- unname(test$estimate)
        p_value <- test$p.value

      } else {

        rho <- NA_real_
        p_value <- NA_real_
      }

      tibble::tibble(
        n = n,
        rho = rho,
        p_value = p_value,
        x_min = min(df$x),
        x_max = max(df$x)
      )
    }
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    x_range = x_max - x_min,

    x_pos = dplyr::if_else(
      is.finite(x_range) & x_range > 0,
      x_max - 0.03 * x_range,
      x_max
    ),

    y_pos = stats_y_pos,

    stat_label = paste0(
      "Spearman \u03c1 = ",
      sprintf("%.2f", rho),
      "\nP = ",
      format.pval(
        p_value,
        digits = 2,
        eps = 0.001
      ),
      ", n = ",
      n
    )
  )


# Inspect correlation results
evo16_scatter_stats %>%
  dplyr::select(
    panel_label,
    n,
    rho,
    p_value
  )
# # A tibble: 8 × 4
#   panel_label                                n    rho p_value
#   <fct>                                  <int>  <dbl>   <dbl>
# 1 "Detrimental\nMedian fitness"             16  0.136  0.616 
# 2 "Strongly detrimental\nMedian fitness"     9 -0.55   0.125 
# 3 "Whole-DMS data\nMinimum fitness"         16 -0.587  0.0168
# 4 "Detrimental\nNumber"                     16  0.407  0.118 
# 5 "Strongly detrimental\nNumber"            16  0.331  0.211 
# 6 "Baseline\nSimilarity (%)"                16 -0.168  0.535 
# 7 "Detrimental\nFraction"                   16  0.429  0.0969
# 8 "Strongly detrimental\nFraction"          16  0.409  0.116 


# ============================================================
# Plot: Mutational features vs. lytic performance
# ============================================================

p_evo16_correlation_panel <-
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    evo16_scatter_plot_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = x,
      y = GrowthRateMin_mean
    )
  ) +

  # Individual viable genomes
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    ggplot2::aes(
      fill = viability_display
    ),
    shape = 21,
    size = 3,
    stroke = 0.6,
    color = "black"
  ) +

  # Spearman statistics
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = evo16_scatter_stats,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = x_pos,
      y = y_pos,
      label = stat_label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 1,
    vjust = 1,
    size = 3.1,
    lineheight = 1.05
  ) +

  # Original colors
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Viable" = "#A8D5A2",
      "Viable after acquired mutation(s)" = "#F2C879"
    ),
    name = NULL
  ) +

  # Shared y-axis range with room for annotations
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      growth_min - 0.03 * growth_range,
      growth_max + 0.20 * growth_range
    ),
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0)
    )
  ) +

  # Four columns, two rows
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(
    ~ panel_label,
    ncol = 4,
    scales = "free_x"
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL,

    y = paste0(
      "Steepest host growth decline\n",
      "(more negative = stronger lytic performance)"
    ),

    title =
      "Associations between mutational metrics and lytic performance"
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme_classic(
    base_size = 11
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",

    strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
      fill = "gray90",
      color = "black",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ),

    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 9.5,
      lineheight = 1.0
    ),

    axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),

    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
      size = 8.5
    ),

    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(
      size = 8.5
    ),

    axis.title.y = ggplot2::element_text(
      size = 10.5
    ),

    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 12
    ),

    plot.title.position = "plot",

    panel.spacing = grid::unit(
      0.35,
      "lines"
    )
  )

print(p_evo16_correlation_panel)
```

### 4) Mutational effects of single-nucleotide substitutions (Fig. S8E)
Include potentially rescuing mutations across genomes viable after acquiring rebooting mutations.
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Heatmap metadata
# ============================================================

# Use the Evo16 dataset for the lytic ranking
evo_lytic_ranking <-
  data_s6[["Evo16_lytic_performance"]] %>%
  dplyr::select(
    isolate,
    lytic_rank_Evo
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(isolate, .keep_all = TRUE)


# Check the similarity-score column name
similarity_col <- "nearest_natural_sequence_similarity"

stopifnot(
  similarity_col %in%
    names(evo300_viability_predictors)
)

# 1) Viable genomes with lytic-performance measurements
heatmap_viable_metadata <-
  evo300_viability_predictors %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    failed_DNA_synthesis == FALSE,
    rebooting_viable %in% TRUE,
    isolate %in% evo_lytic_ranking$isolate
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    original_design_id,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  )

# 2) Nonviable genomes with 98-100% natural similarity
heatmap_nonviable_metadata <-
  evo300_viability_predictors %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    failed_DNA_synthesis == FALSE,
    rebooting_viable %in% FALSE,
    .data[[similarity_col]] >= 98,
    .data[[similarity_col]] <= 100
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    original_design_id,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  )

# 3) Combine metadata
heatmap_metadata <-
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    heatmap_viable_metadata,
    heatmap_nonviable_metadata
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    evo_lytic_ranking,
    by = "isolate"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    heatmap_group = dplyr::if_else(
      rebooting_viable,
      "Viable",
      "Nonviable (98–100% similarity)"
    ),

    heatmap_group = factor(
      heatmap_group,
      levels = c(
        "Viable",
        "Nonviable (98–100% similarity)"
      )
    )
  )

# 4) Unique labels when multiple designs share an isolate
heatmap_metadata <-
  heatmap_metadata %>%
  dplyr::group_by(isolate) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    heatmap_label = dplyr::if_else(
      dplyr::n() == 1,
      isolate,
      paste0(isolate, " | ", original_design_id)
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()


# Viable: order by lytic performance
viable_row_order <-
  heatmap_metadata %>%
  dplyr::filter(rebooting_viable) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(lytic_rank_Evo) %>%

# ============================================================
# Data S6: Rebooting-associated nucleotide changes
# ============================================================

rescued_rebooting_changes <-
  data_s6[["Evo7_rebooting_SNV_changes"]]

# Inspect dataset
dim(rescued_rebooting_changes)
names(rescued_rebooting_changes)
head(rescued_rebooting_changes)

# Check rebooting change types

  rescued_rebooting_changes$rebooting_change,

#               1              24             110

unique(rescued_rebooting_changes$isolate)

# Inspect available DMS-related columns
grep(
  "DMS|fitness|replication|mutation_id",
  names(rescued_rebooting_changes),
  value = TRUE
)


# 1) Standardize rebooting changes
rescued_rebooting_changes <-
  rescued_rebooting_changes %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    rebooting_change_plot = dplyr::case_when(
      rebooting_change %in% c(
        "New mutation",
        "Changed allele"
      ) ~ "New mutation",

      rebooting_change == "Reversion to WT" ~
        "Reversion to WT",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Standardize mutation-effect categories
standardize_DMS_category <- function(x) {

  dplyr::case_when(
    x %in% c(
      "Increased replication",
      "Increased",
      "Beneficial"
    ) ~ "Increased",

    x %in% c(
      "No measurable effect",
      "No effect",
      "Neutral"
    ) ~ "No effect",

    x %in% c(
      "Reduced replication",
      "Detrimental"
    ) ~ "Detrimental",

    x %in% c(
      "Strongly detrimental",
      "Lethal"
    ) ~ "Strongly detrimental",

    TRUE ~ "DMS not covered"
  )
}

# 2) Prepare rebooting events
names(rescued_rebooting_changes)

heatmap_rescue_events <-
  rescued_rebooting_changes %>%

  # Only viable genomes included in the heatmap
  dplyr::semi_join(
    heatmap_metadata %>%
      dplyr::filter(rebooting_viable) %>%
      dplyr::select(original_design_id),
    by = "original_design_id"
  ) %>%

  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(rebooting_change_plot)
  ) %>%

  dplyr::mutate(
    # DMS effect categories
    designed_DMS_category_plot =
      standardize_DMS_category(
        designed_DMS_effect_category
      ),

    recovered_DMS_category_plot =
      standardize_DMS_category(
        recovered_DMS_effect_category
      ),

    # Location of the rebooting symbol
    plot_mutation_id = dplyr::case_when(
      rebooting_change_plot == "Reversion to WT" ~
        designed_mutation_id,

      rebooting_change_plot == "New mutation" ~
        recovered_mutation_id,

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # Genomic position
    genome_position_numeric =
      dplyr::coalesce(
        suppressWarnings(
          as.integer(genome_position)
        ),

        suppressWarnings(
          as.integer(
            stringr::str_extract(
              plot_mutation_id,
              "[0-9]+"
            )
          )
        )
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(plot_mutation_id)
  )

# Inspect
heatmap_rescue_events %>%
  dplyr::select(
    isolate,
    genome_position_numeric,
    designed_mutation_id,
    recovered_mutation_id,
    rebooting_change_plot,
    designed_DMS_replication_score,
    designed_DMS_category_plot,
    recovered_DMS_replication_score,
    recovered_DMS_category_plot
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    isolate,
    genome_position_numeric
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)



# ============================================================
# Designed detrimental mutations
# ============================================================

names(evo300_nt_analysis)

heatmap_designed_damaging <-
  evo300_nt_analysis %>%

  dplyr::semi_join(
    heatmap_metadata %>%
      dplyr::select(original_design_id),
    by = "original_design_id"
  ) %>%

  dplyr::filter(
    mutation_type == "substitution",
    DMS_available
  ) %>%

  dplyr::mutate(
    designed_DMS_category_plot =
      standardize_DMS_category(
        DMS_effect_category_lethal
      )
  ) %>%

  dplyr::filter(
    designed_DMS_category_plot %in% c(
      "Detrimental",
      "Strongly detrimental"
    )
  ) %>%

  dplyr::transmute(
    original_design_id,
    isolate,
    mutation_id,

    genome_position_numeric =
      as.integer(genome_position),

    designed_DMS_fitness =
      DMS_replication_score,

    designed_DMS_category_plot
  ) %>%

  dplyr::distinct(
    original_design_id,
    mutation_id,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  )


# ============================================================
# Designed mutations associated with rebooting changes
# ============================================================

names(heatmap_rescue_events)

heatmap_designed_rebooting_context <-
  heatmap_rescue_events %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(designed_mutation_id)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    original_design_id,
    isolate,

    mutation_id = designed_mutation_id,

    genome_position_numeric =
      dplyr::coalesce(
        suppressWarnings(
          as.integer(genome_position)
        ),

        suppressWarnings(
          as.integer(
            stringr::str_extract(
              designed_mutation_id,
              "[0-9]+"
            )
          )
        )
      ),

    designed_DMS_replication_score,
    designed_DMS_category_plot
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    designed_DMS_fitness = designed_DMS_replication_score
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    original_design_id,
    mutation_id,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  )


# ============================================================
# Combine ordinary detrimental mutations with rebooting-related designed mutations
# ============================================================

heatmap_designed_display <-
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    heatmap_designed_damaging,
    heatmap_designed_rebooting_context
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    original_design_id,
    mutation_id,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  )

# Inspect
heatmap_designed_display %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    isolate == "Evo-Phi5"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(genome_position_numeric) %>%
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)



# ============================================================
# Mutation axis
# ============================================================

heatmap_mutation_axis <-
  dplyr::bind_rows(

    heatmap_designed_display %>%
      dplyr::transmute(
        mutation_id,
        genome_position_numeric
      ),

    heatmap_rescue_events %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        rebooting_change_plot == "New mutation"
      ) %>%
      dplyr::transmute(
        mutation_id = recovered_mutation_id,
        genome_position_numeric
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(mutation_id),
    !is.na(genome_position_numeric)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    mutation_id,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    genome_position_numeric,
    mutation_id
  )

heatmap_mutation_order <-
  heatmap_mutation_axis$mutation_id



# ============================================================
# Complete mutation heatmap matrix
# ============================================================

combined_heatmap_data <-
  tidyr::crossing(
    original_design_id =
      heatmap_metadata$original_design_id,

    mutation_id =
      heatmap_mutation_order
  ) %>%

  dplyr::left_join(
    heatmap_metadata %>%
      dplyr::select(
        original_design_id,
        isolate,
        heatmap_label,
        heatmap_group,
        rebooting_viable,
        lytic_rank_Evo
      ),

    by = "original_design_id",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) %>%

  dplyr::left_join(
    heatmap_designed_display %>%
      dplyr::select(
        original_design_id,
        mutation_id,
        designed_DMS_fitness
      ),

    by = c(
      "original_design_id",
      "mutation_id"
    ),
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) %>%

  dplyr::mutate(
    mutation_id = factor(
      mutation_id,
      levels = heatmap_mutation_order
    ),

    heatmap_label = factor(
      heatmap_label,
      levels = rev(heatmap_row_order)
    )
  )



# ============================================================
# New mutations and reversions
# ============================================================

heatmap_new_mutations <-
  heatmap_rescue_events %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    rebooting_change_plot == "New mutation"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    heatmap_metadata %>%
      dplyr::select(
        original_design_id,
        heatmap_label,
        heatmap_group
      ),

    by = "original_design_id",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    plot_mutation_id = factor(
      recovered_mutation_id,
      levels = heatmap_mutation_order
    ),

    heatmap_label = factor(
      heatmap_label,
      levels = rev(heatmap_row_order)
    ),

    rebooting_symbol = "New mutation"
  )


heatmap_reversions <-
  heatmap_rescue_events %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    rebooting_change_plot == "Reversion to WT"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    heatmap_metadata %>%
      dplyr::select(
        original_design_id,
        heatmap_label,
        heatmap_group
      ),

    by = "original_design_id",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    plot_mutation_id = factor(
      designed_mutation_id,
      levels = heatmap_mutation_order
    ),

    heatmap_label = factor(
      heatmap_label,
      levels = rev(heatmap_row_order)
    ),

    rebooting_symbol = "Reversion to WT"
  )



# ============================================================
# Final heatmap: Designed mutations and rebooting changes (presented Fig. S8E)
# ============================================================

replication_colors <- c(
  "darkred",
  "red",
  "gray88",
  "blue"
)

replication_breaks <- c(
  -1, 0, 1, 1.5
)


p_combined_heatmap_fitness <-
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    combined_heatmap_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = mutation_id,
      y = heatmap_label
    )
  ) +

  # Background cells
  ggplot2::geom_tile(
    fill = "#F5F5F5",
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.12
  ) +

  # Designed mutation replication scores
  ggplot2::geom_tile(
    data = combined_heatmap_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(designed_DMS_fitness)
      ),

    ggplot2::aes(
      fill = designed_DMS_fitness
    ),

    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.12
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = replication_colors,
    values = scales::rescale(replication_breaks),
    limits = c(-1, 1.5),
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = "Replication score"
  ) +

  # New or replacement mutations
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = heatmap_new_mutations %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(recovered_DMS_replication_score)
      ),

    ggplot2::aes(
      x = plot_mutation_id,
      y = heatmap_label,
      color = recovered_DMS_replication_score,
      shape = rebooting_symbol
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 2.5
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_color_gradientn(
    colors = replication_colors,
    values = scales::rescale(replication_breaks),
    limits = c(-1, 1.5),
    oob = scales::squish,
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  # Reversions to WT
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = heatmap_reversions,

    ggplot2::aes(
      x = plot_mutation_id,
      y = heatmap_label,
      shape = rebooting_symbol
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 0.8,
    stroke = 0.4,
    color = "black"
  ) +

  # Symbol legend
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(
      "New mutation" = 16,
      "Reversion to WT" = 4
    ),
    name = "Change during rebooting"
  ) +

  # Viability groups
  ggplot2::facet_grid(
    heatmap_group ~ .,
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +

  # Mutation labels on top
  ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(
    position = "top"
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    title = paste0(
      "Replication effects of designed mutations ",
      "and changes during phage rebooting"
    ),
    x = "Selected nucleotide substitutions",
    y = NULL
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme_classic() +

  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 0,
      vjust = 0.5,
      size = 5
    ),

    axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_text(
      size = 10
    ),

    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(
      size = 8
    ),

    axis.title.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),

    axis.ticks = ggplot2::element_blank(),

    strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
      fill = "gray90",
      color = "black"
    ),

    strip.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 9
    ),

    panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(
      0.4,
      "lines"
    ),

    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical",

    legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 9
    ),

    legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(
      size = 8
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::guides(
    fill = ggplot2::guide_colorbar(
      order = 1,
      barwidth = 10,
      barheight = 1,
      direction = "horizontal",
      ticks.colour = "black",
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5
    ),

    shape = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      order = 2,
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      nrow = 1
    )
  )

print(p_combined_heatmap_fitness)

  #filename = "./plots/p_combined_heatmap_fitness.pdf",
  #plot = p_combined_heatmap_fitness,
  #width = 10,
  #height = 6
#)
```
